pages.text: A hippo child came to play. Excited, the two raced around the bath yard. Dad turned and began calling, "Children—"
Kota's foot slipped! Just before Kota landed on their bottom, Dad caught them under the arms. "Phew... my heart's pounding."
The startled hippo stopped, too. "Why is the floor slippery?" Both looked at their feet.
Dad crouched with them. "Look closely. Slippery stones tell us ahead of time. Shall we find the shiny ones?" Both tilted their heads. "Shiny ones?"
It was true! Only wet stones sparkled in the sun. Dry stones looked pale and calm. Kota pointed. "Found a shiny one!"
"Gentle steps on shiny spots. As you like on pale ones!" They tiptoed over the shiny stones, just like a stepping-stone game.
On dry ground, they raced again. Softly before shiny stones, quickly on pale ones. Kota's tail shot skyward.
"We don't slip now!" The hippo wiggled in a dance. Kota copied. Dad's shoulders shook as he held back laughter.
Now Kota counted aloud at the baths. "One, find shiny spots! Two, gentle steps! Three, fast on pale ground!" Their feet chose the path easily.
That evening, Dad sat beside Kota on the platform, arm around their shoulders. "When the floor says shiny, your feet answer gently." Kota wiggled their toes. "Tomorrow, Shiny Stones, Gentle Steps!"
